events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven pier.** My expectation is a rating of **1 (below average)**, the best of the four. Expect few fish, not a good pier bite.
- **St. Joseph: 1.** Expect a few fish near the piers, not a real pier bite.
- **South Haven: 1 at most, low confidence.** No pier reports at all in the last six weeks.
- **Muskegon: 0 (slow).** Its pier reports have been slow every time.
- If you want better odds this week, I'd fish from a boat. Boat anglers out of Grand Haven did well on the Sept 21 report.

## Why

- Grand Haven pier reports have been slow on every recent report, so I'd expect a 1 at best there, not a 2 or 3.
- The buoy off Grand Haven and Muskegon dropped 21 F in the week before today, a sign of upwelling that Michigan Sea Grant links to salmon moving toward piers. That is why Grand Haven edges out the others, but I'd expect it to help only a little.
- The last upwelling in this season (Aug 17) did not produce a good pier bite at Grand Haven, Muskegon or St. Joseph, so I'd not expect a big jump from this one.
- The Sept 21 Grand Haven boat report rated good (3), with fish 85-140 feet down in 100-200 feet of water, which is why I'd suggest a boat if you can get out safely.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is Sept 21, six days old)
- Grand Haven pier: "Pier anglers found the salmon action to be slow... A few were caught on glow spoons." (Grand Haven, 2022-09-21). The Sept 14 and Sept 7 pier reports were also slow (0).
- Muskegon pier: "No salmon were reported from pier anglers casting spoons." (Muskegon, 2022-09-21). The Sept 7 pier report was also 0.
- St. Joseph: no pier report this season in September. The Sept 14 report said "a couple of boats fishing the pier heads and caught a couple of coho and Chinook" (St. Joseph, 2022-09-14, quality 1).
- South Haven: no pier reports in the last six weeks. Boat reports rated 2 on Sept 14 and 21, with fish mostly on spoons at 110-120+ feet (South Haven, 2022-09-21).
- Boats: Grand Haven rated 3 on Sept 21: "Boat anglers were finding good numbers of immature salmon 85 to 140 feet down in 100 to 200 feet of water." Muskegon boats rated 3 on Sept 21 with white or green fly rotators at 85-130 feet down.

**Past seasons**
- Searching earlier seasons for similar water temperature turned up only one matching week (St. Joseph, 2022-09-21). That is not enough to say what usually happens at the piers in this kind of water, so I have no real historical pier evidence.

**Conditions now** (live data was unavailable, so this is the week-before-today buoy summary)
- Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy 45029): average 62 F, down 21 F over the week, flagged as possible upwelling (Grand Haven and Muskegon, week before 2022-09-27).
- South Haven (buoy 45168): average 67 F, down 6 F, flagged as possible upwelling.
- St. Joseph (buoy 45026): average 67 F, down 4 F.
- No modeled pierhead temperatures were available, so I couldn't check the water right at the piers.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the bite can change quickly in the fall. Treat these ratings as expectations based on old reports.
- The 62 F and 67 F figures are measured offshore buoy readings, not pier water. The upwelling signal is real at the buoy, but I can't confirm it reached the piers.
- Ratings for South Haven and St. Joseph rest on boat reports or thin pier data, so they are lower confidence.
- Wind was not in the data I could get, and wind matters for pier access and safety.

- Sept 14 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32cff90
